sections.title: Habit and flowering
sections.text: The catalogue entry Corylus refers to Corylus avellana, common hazel, often grown as a multi-stemmed coppice. This deciduous shrub or small tree is usually 3–8 m tall and can exceed 10 m. Male catkins hang in late winter; the tiny female flowers are less conspicuous.

sections.title: Hazelnuts
sections.text: The female flowers develop into edible hazelnuts enclosed by a leafy involucre. The plate matches the multi-stemmed habit, catkins and nuts. Corylus colurna, by contrast, is a single-trunk tree with a more deeply divided involucre.
